A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Reward Auditor research. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices A–E support reliable comparison after matching relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original audits of 26 reward models, downstream PPO experiments, and statistical and robustness analyses in Section 5 and appendices B and E.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including reward-model audits, downstream policy-model evaluations, and supplementary analyses.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the confidence and effect-size calculations, and the group-aware rejection procedure remain unchanged. The revised hypotheses and DPO reward identity do not establish a changed implementation or a new audit component.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same RM Bench subsets, Reward Bench Chat, Reward Bench2 Math and Safety, ten perturbation scenarios, and downstream dialogue task. Multimodal auditing appears only as future work in v4.

E2.justification: The evaluated reward-model membership and comparisons with accuracy changes, paired t-tests, and Wilcoxon tests are retained. GPT-5 replaces an evaluation judge, not a competing method.

E3.justification: Section 5.2.1 and Appendix A.2.2 change the reported downstream win-rate judge from GPT-4o to GPT-5, retaining the 100-prompt sample size and judging rubric. This is a stated protocol revision; the PDFs do not establish that evaluations were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix B retains the normality checks, test-statistic sensitivity analysis, skewed-sample comparisons, benchmark comparisons, perturbation clustering, and accuracy-versus-suitability analysis. Figure 12 and its analysis already existed in v2.

E5.justification: The implemented permutation p-value calculation, multiplicity correction, significance thresholds, and confidence-band reporting are retained. No additional repeated-run, seed, or uncertainty-reporting information is introduced; the formal hypothesis revisions are assessed under T1.

E6.justification: The result-table entries and plotted outcomes are unchanged. These include the suitability–policy correlation of -0.881 in Figure 3 and the accuracy–policy correlation of -0.261, with p = 0.4671, in Appendix B.4. The changed judge declaration does not establish a performance gain.

T1.justification: Section 3 replaces distributional equality versus stochastic dominance with mean-difference hypotheses, while Assumption 4.2 separately specifies sign-exchangeability. Definition 3.1 now describes stochastic dominance despite retaining an expectation inequality, and Appendix A Equation 12 adds β to the DPO log-ratio term. Crucially, v4 Equation 5 states E[M−M′] < 0, conflicting with the positive-degradation direction of unchanged Algorithm 1; Appendix C.3 still presents the old distributional hypotheses.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the main claims: suitability measures conditional reliability, Reward Auditor diagnoses vulnerabilities with statistical inference, and suitability risk predicts downstream alignment performance.

C2.justification: The new Limitations and Future Work section identifies dependence on continuous reward scores, difficulty accommodating discrete judge verdicts, and the text-only scope. It proposes rubric-based and multimodal extensions. Section 3 also explains that the suitability margin depends on application-specific tolerance.

D1.justification: Section 5.2.1 newly discloses selecting m as the maximum effect size among the ten models with nonsignificant degradation. Section 3 adds margin-selection guidance, and Appendix A revises the documented DPO scoring formula. These disclosures do not establish changed historical computations.

R1.justification: v4 explicitly attributes Lemma C.2 to Phipson and Smyth and labels Theorem C.4 as adapted from Li and Barber, refining the positioning of existing statistical components. It also adds perturbation, judge, and future-work citations and removes some earlier references, without substantially restructuring the related-work argument.

P1.justification: v4 makes sentence-level grammatical and terminology edits, renames Background to Preliminaries, and moves the paired-data rationale into Section 3. It adds short conflict-of-interest, limitations, and impact sections and updates affiliation and publication text; the overall narrative and appendix structure remain recognizable.

P2.justification: The same twelve figures and seventeen tables remain, with relocation and caption/layout adjustments. Figure 12 moves from a text-wrapped placement in v2 to a standalone placement above Appendix C in v4. The figure graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: v4 improves attribution, documents margin selection, and adds useful applicability limitations. However, the revised central hypothesis conflicts with Algorithm 1 and the unrevised Appendix C.3, while the judge substitution is not reconciled with the unchanged downstream plots. These documentation gains coexist with unresolved theoretical consistency and empirical traceability issues, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
